   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:InventoryPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677880" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Inventories </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Cost is computed using standard cost, which approximates actual cost, on a <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em>-in, <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em>-out basis. Inventories are reduced for write-downs based on periodic reviews for evidence of slow-moving or obsolete parts. The write-down is based on the comparison between inventory on hand and forecasted customer demand for each specific product. Once written down, inventory write-downs are <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> reversed until the inventory is sold or scrapped. Inventory write-downs are also established when conditions indicate the net realizable value is less than cost due to physical deterioration, technological obsolescence, changes in price level or other causes.&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:IntangibleAssetsFiniteLivedPolicy" id="c56677882" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Intangible Assets</b></p> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">Intangible assets represent rights acquired for developed technology, customer relationships, trademarks, patents and in-process research and development (&#x201c;IPR&amp;D&#x201d;) in connection with business acquisitions. Intangible assets with finite useful lives are amortized over periods ranging from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674459">one</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674460">ten</span> years using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits of the intangible asset are consumed, or if that pattern cannot be reliably determined, using a straight-line amortization method. Acquired IPR&amp;D is capitalized and amortization commences upon completion of the underlying projects. If any of the projects are abandoned, the Company would be required to impair the related IPR&amp;D asset.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Impairment of Long-lived Assets and Goodwill</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i></i></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677883" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Long-lived Assets </i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company assesses the impairment of long-lived assets, which consist primarily of property and equipment and intangible assets, whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that such assets might be impaired and the carrying value <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recoverable. Events or changes in circumstances that <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>indicate that an asset is impaired include significant decreases in the market value of an asset, significant underperformance relative to expected historical or projected future results of operations, a change in the extent or manner in which an asset is utilized, significant declines in the estimated fair value of the overall Company for a sustained period, shifts in technology, loss of key management or personnel, changes in the Company&#x2019;s operating model or strategy and competitive forces.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">If events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recoverable and the expected undiscounted future cash flows attributable to the asset are less than the carrying amount of the asset, an impairment loss equal to the excess of the asset&#x2019;s carrying value over its fair value is recorded. Fair value is determined based on the present value of estimated expected future cash flows using a discount rate commensurate with the risk involved, quoted market prices or appraised values, depending on the nature of the asset.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p>
   <ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>

    </div> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Inphi Corporation</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>(Dollars in thousands except share and per share amounts)</b></p></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i></i></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy" id="c56677884" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Goodwill </i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Goodwill is recorded when consideration paid for a business acquisition exceeds the fair value of net tangible and intangible assets acquired. Goodwill is measured and tested for impairment on an annual basis during the <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">fourth</em> fiscal quarter or more frequently if the Company believes indicators of impairment exist. &#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">To review for impairment, the Company <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> assesses qualitative factors to determine whether events or circumstances lead to a determination that it is more likely than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the fair value of its reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. The qualitative assessment of the recoverability of goodwill, whether performed annually or based on specific events or circumstances, considers various macroeconomic, industry-specific and company-specific factors. Those factors include: (i) severe adverse industry or economic trends; (ii) significant company-specific actions, including exiting an activity in conjunction with restructuring of operations; (iii) current, historical or projected deterioration of its financial performance; or (iv) a sustained decrease in its market capitalization below its net book value. After assessing the totality of events and circumstances, if the Company determines that it is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> more likely than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the fair value of&#xa0;its reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> further assessment is performed. If however, the Company determines that it is more likely than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the fair value of the reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to the excess. There was <ix:nonFraction id="c56674471" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" scale="0">no</ix:nonFraction> impairment of goodwill in <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019,</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em>&#xa0;&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:InternalUseSoftwarePolicy" id="c56677885" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Internal Use Software Costs</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Certain external computer software costs acquired for internal use are capitalized. Training costs and maintenance are expensed as incurred, while upgrades and enhancements are capitalized if it is probable that such expenditures will result in additional functionality. Capitalized costs are included within property and equipment. If a cloud computing arrangement includes a software license, then the Company accounts for the software license element of the arrangement consistent with the acquisition of other software licenses. If a cloud computing arrangement does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> include a software license, the Company accounts for the arrangement as a service contract.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677886" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Revenue Recognition</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Prior to <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>the Company recognized revenue when there was persuasive evidence of an arrangement, delivery had occurred, the fee was fixed or determinable, and collection was reasonably assured.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">On <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>the Company adopted Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606</em>), using the modified retrospective method applied to those contracts which were <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> completed as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018. </em>The adoption of this guidance resulted in <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> cumulative effect adjustment as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018. </em>Starting <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>the Company recognizes revenue on sales to distributors upon shipment and transfer of control (known as &#x201c;sell-in&#x201d; revenue recognition), rather than deferring recognition until distributors report that they have sold the products to their customers (known as &#x201c;sell-through&#x201d; revenue recognition). The impact of the adoption on revenue and cost of revenue for the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018&#xa0;</em>was an increase of $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674481" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" scale="3">3,778</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674482" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold" scale="3">779</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. Deferred revenue and inventories decreased by $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674483" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:DeferredRevenue" scale="3">3,778</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674484" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:InventoryNet" scale="3">779</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018, </em>respectively. Results for reporting periods beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>are presented under the new revenue guidance, while prior periods were <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> retrospectively adjusted and continue to be reported in accordance with the Company&#x2019;s historic revenue recognition accounting.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">The following table shows revenue by geography, based on the receiving location of customers:</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>

    </ix:nonNumeric> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">The Company recognizes revenue when control of the promised goods or services is transferred to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects to receive in exchange for such goods or services.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;"></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>

     </div> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Inphi Corporation</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>(Dollars in thousands except share and per share amounts)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Product Revenue</i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:22.5pt;">The Company&#x2019;s products are fully functional at the time of shipment and do <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> require additional production, modification, or customization. The Company recognizes revenue upon transfer of control at a point in time when title transfers either upon shipment to or receipt by the customer, net of accruals for estimated sales returns and allowances. Sales and other taxes the Company collects are excluded from revenue. The fee is based on specific products and quantities to be delivered at specified prices, which is evidenced by a customer purchase order or other evidence of an arrangement. Certain distributors <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>receive a credit for price discounts associated with the distributors' customers that purchased those products. The Company estimates the extent of these distributor price discounts at each reporting period to reduce accounts receivable and revenue. Although the Company accrues an estimate of distributor price discounts, the Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> issue these discounts to the distributor until the inventory is sold to the distributors' customers. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em>&#xa0;and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> the estimated price discount was $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674490" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerRefundLiability" scale="3">656</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674491" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerRefundLiability" scale="3">1,634</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. Payment terms of customers are typically <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">30</em> to <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">60</em> days after invoice date. The Company&#x2019;s products are under warranty against defects in material and workmanship generally for a period of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674494">one</span> or <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674495">two</span> years. The Company accrues for estimated warranty costs at the time of sale based on anticipated warranty claims and actual historical warranty claims experience including knowledge of specific product failures that are outside of the Company&#x2019;s typical experience.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Other Revenue</i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:27pt;">Occasionally, the Company enters into license and development agreements with some of its customers and recognizes revenue from these agreements upon completion and acceptance by the customer of contract deliverables or as services are provided, depending on the terms of the arrangement. Revenue is deferred for any amounts billed or received prior to transfer of control. The Company believes the milestone&#xa0;method&#xa0;best depicts the efforts expended to transfer services to the customers&#xa0;under most of the Company&#x2019;s development agreements. Certain contracts <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>include multiple performance obligations for which the Company allocates revenues to each performance obligation based on relative stand-alone selling price. The Company determines stand-alone selling prices based on&#xa0;observable evidence.&#xa0; When stand-alone selling prices are <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> directly observable, the Company uses the adjusted market assessment approach or residual approach, if applicable.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:27pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:27pt;">The Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> disclose the value of unsatisfied performance obligations for (i) contracts with an original expected length of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674571"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674572">one</span></span></em> year or less or (ii) contracts for which the Company recognizes revenue at the amount to which it has the right to invoice for services performed.&#xa0; The estimated revenue expected to be recognized in <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2020</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2021</em>&#xa0;related to performance obligations that are unsatisfied (or partially unsatisfied) as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019 </em>was $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674501" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionStartDateAxis-RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionStartDateAxis.domain-2020-01-01" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation" scale="3">12,338</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674502" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionStartDateAxis-RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionStartDateAxis.domain-2021-01-01" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" name="us-gaap:RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation" scale="3">7,790</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Revenue from non-product sales was approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c56674503" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-LicensesForIntellectualPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2" name="iphi:PercentOfRevenueFromNonproductSales" scale="-2">7</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction id="c56674504" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-LicensesForIntellectualPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2" name="iphi:PercentOfRevenueFromNonproductSales" scale="-2">3</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c56674505" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31_ProductOrServiceAxis-LicensesForIntellectualPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2" name="iphi:PercentOfRevenueFromNonproductSales" scale="-2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of total revenue for the years ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019, </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>, respectively.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company monitors the collectability of accounts receivable primarily through review of the accounts receivable aging. The Company&#x2019;s policy is to record an allowance for doubtful accounts based on specific collection issues identified, aging of underlying receivables and historical experience of uncollectible balances.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:CostOfSalesPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677887" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Cost of Revenue</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Cost of revenue includes cost of materials, such as wafers processed by <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party foundries, cost associated with packaging and assembly, testing and shipping, cost of personnel, including stock-based compensation, and equipment associated with manufacturing support, logistics and quality assurance, warranty cost, amortization and impairment of developed technology, amortization of step-up values of inventory, write-down of inventories, amortization of production mask costs, overhead and occupancy costs.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:StandardProductWarrantyPolicy" id="c56677888" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Warranty</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company&#x2019;s products are under warranty against defects in material and workmanship generally for a period of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> or <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> years. The Company accrues for estimated warranty cost at the time of sale based on anticipated warranty claims and actual historical warranty claims experience including knowledge of specific product failures that are outside of the Company&#x2019;s typical experience. The warranty obligation is determined based on product failure rates, cost of replacement and failure analysis cost. If actual warranty costs differ significantly from these estimates, adjustments <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be required in the future. As of both <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em>, the warranty liability was immaterial.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c56677889" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Research and Development Expense</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Research and development expense consists of costs incurred in performing research and development activities including salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits, occupancy costs, pre-production engineering mask costs, impairment of in-process research and development, overhead costs and prototype wafer, packaging and test costs. Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. The Company enters into development agreements with some of the Company&#x2019;s customers. Recoveries from nonrecurring engineering services from early stage technology are recorded as an offset to product development expense incurred in support of this effort and serve as a mechanism to partially recover development expenditures. These reimbursements are recognized upon completion and acceptance by the customer of contract deliverables or milestones. The Company recorded approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674512" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="iphi:ReimbursementsFromResearchAndDevelopmentContracts" scale="3">0</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674513" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="iphi:ReimbursementsFromResearchAndDevelopmentContracts" scale="3">0</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674514" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6" name="iphi:ReimbursementsFromResearchAndDevelopmentContracts" scale="3">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;as offset to research and development expense for the years ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019, </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>, respectively.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="iphi:SellingAndMarketingPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677890" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Sales and Marketing Expense </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Sales and marketing expense consists of salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits, travel, trade show costs, amortization of intangibles and others. Advertising expenses for the years ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019, </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> were <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> material.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677891" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>General and Administrative Expense </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">General and administrative expense consists of salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits and expenses for executive management, legal, finance and others. In addition, general and administrative expense includes fees for professional services and occupancy costs. These costs are expensed as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677892" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on differences between financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities, and are measured using the enacted tax rates and laws that will be in effect when the differences are expected to reverse. The Company recognizes the deferred income tax effects of a change in tax rates in the period of enactment. The Company must also make judgments in evaluating whether deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income. To the extent that it believes that recovery is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> likely, the Company must establish a valuation allowance. The carrying value of the Company&#x2019;s net deferred tax asset is based on whether it is more likely than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the Company will generate sufficient future taxable income to realize these deferred tax assets. A valuation allowance is established for deferred tax assets which the Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> believe meet the &#x201c;more likely than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not&#x201d;</em> criteria. The Company&#x2019;s judgments regarding future taxable income <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>change over time due to changes in market conditions, changes in tax laws, tax planning strategies or other factors. If the Company&#x2019;s assumptions and consequently its estimates change in the future, the valuation allowance the Company has established <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be increased or decreased, resulting in a material respective increase or decrease in income tax expense (benefit) and related impact on the Company&#x2019;s reported net income (loss).</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company regularly performs a comprehensive review of uncertain tax positions. An uncertain tax position represents an expected treatment of a tax position taken in a filed tax return, or planned to be taken in a future tax return or claim, which has <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been reflected in measuring income tax expense for financial reporting purposes. Until these positions are sustained by the taxing authorities, the Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> recognize the tax benefits resulting from such positions and reports the tax effects as a liability for uncertain tax positions in the consolidated financial statements. The Company recognizes potential interest and penalties on uncertain tax positions within the provision (benefit) for income taxes on the consolidated statement of income (loss).</p> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">On <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 22, 2017, </em>the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#x201c;Tax Reform Act&#x201d;) was signed into law. The Tax Reform Act contains significant changes to U.S. federal corporate income taxation, including a reduction of the corporate tax rate from <ix:nonFraction id="c56674527" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31" unitRef="Pure" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2" name="iphi:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtHighestFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRatePercent" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c56674528" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="Pure" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction>% effective <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>a <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-time transition tax on deemed mandatory repatriation of accumulated earnings and profits of foreign subsidiaries in conjunction with the elimination of U.S. tax on dividend distributions from foreign subsidiaries, and a temporary <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">100%</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em>-year depreciation deduction for certain capital investments. The effect of the tax law changes must be recognized in the period of enactment. As a result of the change in tax rate, the Company's deferred tax assets and liabilities were required to be remeasured to reflect their value at a lower tax rate of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">21%.</em> Staff Accounting Bulletin <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118</em> (&#x201c;SAB <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118&#x201d;</em>) allows for a measurement period of up to <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year after the enactment date of the new tax legislation to finalize the recording of the related tax impacts. In accordance with SAB <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">118,</em> as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the Company made a provisional estimate of the remeasurement of the federal deferred tax assets and liabilities to reflect the reduced U.S. statutory corporate tax rate to <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">21%,</em> the mandatory repatriation income which was fully absorbed by the U.S. net operating loss, the related valuation allowance offset, and valuation allowance release on deferred tax assets for the federal alternative minimum tax (&#x201c;AMT&#x201d;) credit that was made refundable by the Tax Reform Act. During <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> the Company elected to account for&#xa0;global intangible low-taxed income (&#x201c;GILTI&#x201d;) as a period cost in the year the tax is incurred and made changes to its provisional estimates previously recorded for the mandatory repatriation upon filing of its <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> U.S. income tax return. The change in the mandatory repatriation income was fully absorbed by the U.S. net operating loss, which is subject to valuation allowance, and resulted in <ix:nonFraction id="c56674540" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017TransitionTaxForAccumulatedForeignEarningsLiability" scale="0">no</ix:nonFraction> current tax liability. This measurement period adjustment had <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> net tax effect after the offsetting change to the valuation allowance. At <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018, </em>the Company completed the accounting for all of the enactment-date income tax effects of the Tax Reform Act.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c56677893" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Stock-Based Compensation </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Stock-based compensation for stock option and restricted stock units issued to the Company&#x2019;s employees is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as expense over the requisite service period, which is the vesting period, on a straight-line basis&#xa0;or graded vesting basis for awards with performance or market-based conditions. The fair value of restricted stock units is based on the fair market value of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of grant. If the award has a market condition, the Company estimates the fair value using Monte Carlo simulation model and recognizes compensation&#xa0;ratably over the service period.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company has elected to treat share-based payment awards with graded vesting schedules and time-based service conditions as single awards and recognizes stock-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis (net of estimated forfeitures) over the requisite service period.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company recognizes non-employee stock-based compensation expense&#xa0;based on the estimated fair value of the equity instrument determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model or fair value of the Company's common stock. Management believes that the fair value of the underlying stock award is more reliably measured than the fair value of the services received. The fair value of each non-employee variable stock award is re-measured each period until a commitment date is reached, which is generally the vesting date.&#xa0;&#xa0;Starting <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019,&#xa0;</em>the Company adopted&#xa0;the new guidance for equity-classified share-based payment awards issued to nonemployees,&#xa0;and therefore <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer remeasures awards each period until a commitment date is reached.&#xa0; The stock-based compensation&#xa0;expense is measured on the grant date. The Company recognizes compensation cost for awards with performance conditions when achievement of those conditions are probable, rather than upon their achievement.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c56677894" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Earnings per Share </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">Basic earnings per share is calculated by dividing income allocable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per share is calculated by dividing the net income allocable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding, adjusted for the effects of potentially dilutive common stock, which are comprised of stock options, restricted stock units, employee share purchase plan and the shares that could be issued upon conversion of the Company&#x2019;s convertible debt. The capped call options in connection with the issuance of the convertible notes are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share as their impact is always anti-dilutive.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677895" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Segment Information </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company operates in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674544"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674573"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56674574">one</span></span></span> reportable segment related to the design, development and sale of high-speed analog connectivity components that operate to maintain, amplify and improve signal integrity at high-speeds in a wide variety of applications. The Company&#x2019;s chief operating decision-maker is its Chief Executive Officer, who reviews&#xa0;financial and operational information on a consolidated basis&#xa0;for the purpose&#xa0;of evaluating relative performance, progress against strategic objectives and making decisions about investing resources.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

    </div> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Inphi Corporation</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>(Dollars in thousands except share and per share amounts)</b></p></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c56677896" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2016, </em>the&#xa0;Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201c;FASB&#x201d;) issued guidance that requires companies that lease assets (lessees) to recognize on the balance sheet the assets and liabilities for the rights and obligations created by leases with lease terms of more than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em> months. The FASB also issued additional updates to such guidance. For leases less than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">twelve</em> months, an entity is permitted to make an accounting policy election by class of underlying asset <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to recognize lease assets and lease liabilities. If a lessee makes this election, it should recognize lease expense for such leases generally on a straight-line basis over the lease term. The guidance requires entities to recognize and measure leases at the beginning of the earliest period presented using a modified retrospective approach or allows entities to initially apply the new lease standard at the adoption date and recognize a cumulative-effect adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings in the period of adoption. The Company adopted this guidance on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>See note <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7</em>&#xa0;in the notes to consolidated financial statements for further details.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 2016, </em>the FASB issued guidance which requires the credit losses related to debt securities classified as available-for sale to be presented as an allowance rather than as a write-down.&#xa0;&#xa0;The guidance also requires that an entity measure and recognize expected credit losses for financial assets held at amortized cost and replaces the incurred loss impairment methodology in current GAAP with a methodology that requires consideration of a broader range of information to estimate credit losses.&#xa0;&#xa0;This guidance is effective for the Company beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019. </em>The adoption of this guidance is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to have a material impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017, </em>the FASB issued guidance to simplify the measurement of goodwill by eliminating the Step <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> impairment test. Step <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> measures a goodwill impairment loss by comparing the implied fair value of a reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill with the carrying amount of that goodwill. The guidance requires an entity to compare the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount and recognize an impairment charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value. Additionally, an entity should consider income tax effects from any tax deductible goodwill on the carrying amount of the reporting unit when measuring the goodwill impairment loss, if applicable. The guidance becomes effective for goodwill impairment tests in fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019, </em>though early adoption is permitted. The Company adopted this guidance on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>The adoption of this standard did <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;"></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>
     <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
      <div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
       <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">59</em>
      </div>

     </div> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Inphi Corporation</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>(Dollars in thousands except share and per share amounts)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2018, </em>the FASB issued guidance that allows an option to reclassify from accumulated other comprehensive income to retained earnings any stranded tax effects resulting from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the "Tax Act"). The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018.&#xa0;&#xa0;</em>The Company adopted this guidance on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>The adoption of this standard did <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 2018, </em>the FASB issued guidance to eliminate the separate guidance applicable to share-based payments to nonemployees. Under the new guidance, equity-classified share-based payment awards issued to nonemployees will be measured on the grant date, instead of being remeasured through the performance completion date (generally the vesting date), as required under the current guidance. The guidance also requires recognition of compensation cost for awards with performance conditions when achievement of those conditions are probable, rather than upon their achievement. Further, the guidance eliminates the requirement to reassess the classification of nonemployee awards under the financial instruments literature upon vesting. The guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018. </em>The Company adopted this guidance on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>The adoption of this standard did <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2018, </em>the FASB issued guidance that eliminates certain disclosure requirements for fair value measurements for all entities, requires public entities to disclose certain new information and modifies some disclosure requirements. The new guidance will <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer require disclosure of the amount of and reasons for transfers between Level <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> and Level <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> of the fair value hierarchy, but will require disclosure of the range and weighted average used to develop significant unobservable inputs for Level <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em> fair value measurements. The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019. </em>The adoption of this guidance is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to have a material impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2018, </em>the FASB issued guidance requiring a customer in a cloud computing arrangement that is a service contract to follow the internal use software guidance in Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">350</em>-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">40</em> to determine which implementation costs to capitalize as assets. Capitalized implementation costs are expensed over the term of the hosting arrangement beginning when the module or component of the hosting arrangement is ready for its intended use. The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019. </em>The adoption of this guidance is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to have a material impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 2018, </em>the FASB issued amendments to guidance on &#x201c;Collaborative Arrangements&#x201d; and &#x201c;Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#x201d;, that require transactions in collaborative arrangements to be accounted for under &#x201c;Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#x201d; if the counterparty is a customer for a good or service (or bundle of goods and services) that is a distinct unit of account. The amendments also preclude entities from presenting consideration from transactions with a collaborator that is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> a customer together with revenue recognized from contracts with customers. The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019.&#xa0; </em>The adoption of this guidance is <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to have a material impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 2019, </em>the FASB issued guidance that simplifies the accounting for income taxes as part of FASB's overall initiative to reduce complexity in accounting standards.&#xa0; Amendments include removal of certain exceptions to the general principles of ASC <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740,</em> Income Taxes, and simplification in general other areas such as accounting for a franchise tax (or similar tax) that is partially based on income.&#xa0; The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2020, </em>though early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that this new guidance will have on its consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

This investment is presented within&#xa0;other assets, net on the consolidated balance sheet.&#xa0; During the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019, </em>the Company sold a&#xa0;marketable equity investment in a company located in the United States acquired in the same year for $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674627" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromSaleAndMaturityOfOtherInvestments" scale="3">3,424</ix:nonFraction>.&#xa0; The gain on sale of $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674628" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-OtherIncomeMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:GainOnSaleOfInvestments" scale="3">924</ix:nonFraction> was included in other income, net in the consolidated statements of income (loss).</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#xa0; &#xa0; &#xa0; &#xa0; &#xa0; The Company has non-marketable equity investments in privately held companies without readily determinable market values. Prior to <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>the Company accounted for non-marketable equity investments at cost less impairment. Realized gains and losses on non-marketable equity investments sold or impaired were recognized in other income, net. On <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>the Company adopted ASU <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01,</em> Financial Instruments &#x2013; Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities, which changed the way the Company accounts for non-marketable equity investments. The Company adjusts the carrying value of non-marketable equity investments to fair value upon observable transactions for identical or similar investments of the same issuer or impairment (referred to as the measurement alternative). All gains and losses on non-marketable equity investments, realized and unrealized, are recognized in other income, net. There was <ix:nonFraction id="c56674631" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201601Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:CumulativeEffectOfNewAccountingPrincipleInPeriodOfAdoption" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> cumulative effect adjustment upon adoption of this guidance. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em>, non-marketable equity investments had a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674632" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3">25,792</ix:nonFraction>, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674633" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember_FinancialInstrumentAxis-EquitySecuritiesFairValueBasedOnObservableTransactionMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3">8,792</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;was remeasured to fair value based on observable transaction during the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em>. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018,&#xa0;</em>non-marketable equity investments had a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674634" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3">16,866</ix:nonFraction>, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674635" contextRef="i_2018-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherNoncurrentAssetsMember_FinancialInstrumentAxis-EquitySecuritiesFairValueBasedOnObservableTransactionMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3">6,066</ix:nonFraction> was remeasured to fair value based on observable transaction during the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018.&#xa0; </em>These investments are presented within other assets, net on the consolidated balance sheets. The unrealized gain recorded in other income, net and included as adjustment to the carrying value of non-marketable equity investments held was $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674636" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueUpwardPriceAdjustmentAnnualAmount" scale="3">1,926</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674637" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueUpwardPriceAdjustmentAnnualAmount" scale="3">3,066</ix:nonFraction> for the years ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> respectively.&#xa0;During the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018, </em>the Company recorded an impairment charge of&#xa0;$<ix:nonFraction id="c56674639" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueImpairmentLossAnnualAmount" scale="3">7,000</ix:nonFraction> related to a certain investment in a private company because the investee was in receivership and the Company was <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to recover its cost.&#xa0;&#xa0;The impairment charge was included in other income, net in the consolidated statements of income (loss).</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em></b><b>. Concentrations </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">Financial instruments that subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash, cash equivalents, investments in marketable securities and trade accounts receivable. The Company extends differing levels of credit to customers and does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> require collateral deposits.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">During the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the Company abandoned a project related to certain developed technology and in-process research and development from the ClariPhy Communications, Inc. (ClariPhy) acquisition resulting in an impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674831" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ClariPhyCommunicationsIncmember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsExcludingGoodwill" scale="3">47,014</ix:nonFraction>, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674832" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ClariPhyCommunicationsIncmember_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-CostOfSalesMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsExcludingGoodwill" scale="3">10,174</ix:nonFraction> was included in the cost of revenue and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674833" contextRef="d_2017-01-01_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ClariPhyCommunicationsIncmember_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-ResearchAndDevelopmentExpenseMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsExcludingGoodwill" scale="3">36,840</ix:nonFraction> was included in the research and development expenses in the consolidated statements of income (loss). The abandonment of the project was primarily related to the change in product roadmap that occurred during the year ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017.</em></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeasesTextBlock" id="c1446668" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7.</em> Leases </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019, </em>the Company adopted Accounting Standards Update (&#x201c;ASU&#x201d;) <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> Leases (Topic <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842</em>), using the modified retrospective method&#xa0;through a cumulative adjustment to the beginning accumulated deficit balance. Prior comparative periods have <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been restated under this method. The adoption of this guidance resulted in <ix:nonFraction id="c56674924" contextRef="i_2019-01-01_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:CumulativeEffectOfNewAccountingPrincipleInPeriodOfAdoption" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> cumulative effect adjustment as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019.&#xa0; </em>However, total assets and liabilities increased by $<ix:nonFraction id="c56674925" contextRef="i_2019-01-01_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3">10,670</ix:nonFraction> as a result of the adoption. Based on the new guidance, for leases less than <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">twelve</em> months, an entity is permitted to make an accounting policy election by class of underlying asset <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to recognize lease assets and lease liabilities. If a lessee makes this election, it should recognize lease expense for such leases generally on a straight-line basis over the lease term. The Company made this election, along with other available practical expedients. This guidance had a material impact on the&#xa0;consolidated balance sheets as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019, </em>but did <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have an impact on the consolidated statements of income (loss) and cash flows. The most significant impact was the recognition of right of use (&#x201c;ROU&#x201d;) asset and lease liabilities for operating leases related to facility leases.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception. Operating leases are included in operating lease ROU assets, other current liabilities and other long-term liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. Finance leases are included in property and equipment, other current liabilities, and other long-term liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. As of the adoption date and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019, </em>the Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have material finance leases.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are recognized based on the present value of the future minimum lease payments over the lease term at commencement date. As most of the leases do <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> provide an implicit rate, the Company uses the incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at commencement date in determining the present value of future payments. The operating lease ROU asset also includes any lease payments and initial direct costs incurred, net of lease incentives. The lease terms <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise the&#xa0;option. Lease expense for minimum lease payments is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. The Company has lease agreements with lease and non-lease components, which are generally accounted for separately.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#xa0;</p>
