   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b>(Dollars in thousands except share and per share amounts)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:27pt;">The Company measures its investments in marketable securities at fair value using the market approach which uses prices and other relevant information generated by market transactions involving identical or comparable assets or liabilities. The Company has cash equivalents which consist of money market funds valued using the amortized cost method, in accordance with Rule <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2a</em>-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7</em> under the <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1940</em> Act which approximates fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:27pt;">The convertible notes are carried on the consolidated balance sheets at their original issuance value including accreted interest, net of unamortized debt discount and issuance costs. The Convertible Notes are <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> marked to fair value at the end of each reporting period. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em>, the fair value of Convertible Notes was determined on the basis of market prices observable for similar instruments and is considered Level <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> in the fair value hierarchy. The fair value of the Convertible Notes as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c56675700" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" scale="3">845,296</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c56675701" contextRef="i_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" scale="3">512,428</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p>

As discussed in Note <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2,</em> the Company has non-marketable equity investments which are classified within Level <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em> in the fair value hierarchy.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em></b><b><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6</em></b><b>. Commitments and Contingencies </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Leases </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">The Company has noncancelable service agreements, including software licenses, colocation and cloud services used in research and development activities expiring in various years through <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2024.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Noncancelable Purchase Obligations </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;The Company depends upon <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> party subcontractors to manufacture wafers. The Company&#x2019;s subcontractor relationships typically allow for the cancellation of outstanding purchase orders, but require payment of all expenses incurred through the date of cancellation. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em>, the total value of open purchase orders for wafers was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c56675809" contextRef="i_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="iphi:ValueOfOpenPurchaseOrders" scale="3">14,977</ix:nonFraction>. As of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em>, the Company has a commitment to pay mask costs o<span style="background-color:null;">f $<ix:nonFraction id="c56675810" contextRef="i_2019-12-31_LongTermPurchaseCommitmentByCategoryOfItemPurchasedAxis-MaskMember" unitRef="USD" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:PurchaseObligation" scale="3">542</ix:nonFraction>.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Legal Proceedings </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Netlist, Inc. v. Inphi Corporation, Case <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em>&#xa0;<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em>-cv-<em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6900</em> (C.D. Cal.) </i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt -2pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">On <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> September 22, 2009, </em>Netlist filed suit in the United States District Court, Central District of California (the &#x201c;Court&#x201d;),&#xa0;asserting that the Company infringes U.S. Patent <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,532,537.</em> Netlist filed an amended complaint on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 22, 2009, </em>further&#xa0;asserting that the Company infringes U.S. Patent Nos. <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,619,912</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,636,274,</em> collectively with U.S. Patent <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,532,537,</em> the&#xa0;patents-in-suit, and seeking both unspecified monetary damages to be determined and an injunction to prevent further&#xa0;infringement. These infringement claims allege that the iMB&#x2122; and certain other memory module components infringe the patents in-suit. The Company answered the amended complaint on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 11, 2010 </em>and asserted that the Company does <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> infringe the&#xa0;patents-in-suit and that the patents-in-suit are invalid. In <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2010,</em> the Company filed inter partes requests for reexamination with the&#xa0;United States Patent and Trademark Office (the &#x201c;USPTO&#x201d;), asserting that the patents-in-suit are invalid. As a result of the&#xa0;proceedings at the USPTO, the Court has stayed the litigation, with the parties advising the Court on status every <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">120</em> days.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">As to the proceeding at the USPTO, reexamination has been ordered for all of the patents that Netlist alleged to infringe. At&#xa0;present, the USPTO has determined that almost all of the originally filed claims are <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> valid, and determined certain amended&#xa0;claims to be patentable. The Reexamination Certificate for U.S. Patent <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,532,537</em> was issued on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2, 2016 </em>based on&#xa0;amended claims. The Reexamination Certificate for U.S. Patent <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,636,274</em> was issued on <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 5, 2018, </em>indicating that all&#xa0;claims, <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> through <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">97,</em> were cancelled. The parties continue to assert their respective positions with respect to the reexamination&#xa0;proceeding for U.S. Patent <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7,619,912.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">While the Company intends to defend the foregoing USPTO proceedings and lawsuit vigorously, the USPTO proceedings&#xa0;and litigation, whether or <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> determined in the Company&#x2019;s favor or settled, could be costly and time-consuming and could divert&#xa0;management&#x2019;s attention and resources, which could adversely affect the Company&#x2019;s business.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">Due to the nature of USPTO proceedings and litigation, the Company is currently unable to predict the final outcome of this&#xa0;lawsuit and therefore cannot determine the likelihood of loss nor estimate a range of possible loss. However, because of the nature&#xa0;and inherent uncertainties of litigation, should the outcome of these actions be unfavorable, the Company&#x2019;s business, financial&#xa0;condition, results of operations or cash flows could be materially and adversely affected.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Claims Against eSilicon Corporation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">In connection with the Company's&#xa0;acquisition of eSilicon Corporation (&#x201c;eSilicon&#x201d;) as discussed in Note <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">17,</em> eSilicon and the Company have received written communications from certain former stockholders of eSilicon demanding to inspect eSilicon&#x2019;s books and records and indicating that such stockholders will be seeking appraisal of shares they held in eSilicon. Certain of these former eSilicon stockholders also have stated that they <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>assert claims against eSilicon&#x2019;s directors and senior officers for alleged breaches of fiduciary duty and other violations in connection with the merger between eSilicon and a subsidiary of the Company.&#xa0; The Company is unaware of any petition for appraisal and/or lawsuit being filed by any former eSilicon stockholder.&#xa0; The Company believes that the claims in such written communications are without merit, and plan to vigorously defend against lawsuits arising out of or relating to the merger agreement and/or the merger that <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be filed in the future.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Indemnifications </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">In the ordinary course of business, the Company <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>provide indemnifications of varying scope and terms to customers, vendors, lessors, investors, directors, officers, employees and other parties with respect to certain matters, including, but <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> limited to, losses arising out of the Company&#x2019;s breach of such agreements, services to be provided by the Company, or from intellectual property infringement claims made by <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-parties. These indemnifications <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>survive termination of the underlying agreement and the maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification provisions <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be subject to maximum loss clauses. The Company has <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> incurred material costs to defend lawsuits or settle claims related to these indemnifications. Accordingly, the Company has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56675839"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c56675840">no</span></span> liabilities recorded for these agreements as of <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2019</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2018</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:justify;">As further described in note <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1,</em> in connection with the preparation of the Company&#x2019;s <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> year-end audited consolidated financial statements, the Company identified a&#xa0;classification error in its previously filed unaudited interim condensed consolidated statements of cash flows for the three, <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 31, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 31, 2018, </em><em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> September 30, 2019 </em>and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> September 30, 2018, </em>respectively. Specifically, it was determined that payments made under the Company&#x2019;s multi-year agreements for the purchase of internal use intangible&#xa0;assets should have been classified as use of cash for financing activities and <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> as use of cash for investing activities as originally presented.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:justify;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.2pt;text-align:justify;">Management has concluded that such classification error did <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> result in the previously issued unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements being materially misstated. The Company will, however, revise the <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> unaudited quarterly condensed consolidated statements of cash flows in connection with the future filings of its <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2020</em> Form <em style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em>-Qs to correct for such classification error.&#xa0;&#xa0;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">(a) <i>Evaluation of disclosure controls and procedures</i>. We maintain &#x201c;disclosure controls and procedures,&#x201d; as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15 (e) and 15d &#x2013; 15(e) under the Exchange Act, that are designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by us in reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#x2019;s rules and forms and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (principal executive officer) and Chief Financial Officer (principal financial officer), as appropriate, to allow for timely decisions regarding required disclosure. In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the disclosure controls and procedures are met. Our disclosure controls and procedures have been designed to provide reasonable, not absolute assurance. Additionally, in designing disclosure controls and procedures, our management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible disclosure controls and procedures. The design of any disclosure controls and procedures also is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&#xa0;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">Based on their evaluation as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, as of such date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">(b)&#xa0;<i>Management&#x2019;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting.</i>&#xa0;&#xa0;Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f). Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with policies or procedures may deteriorate. Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019. In making this assessment, our management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission in <i>Internal Control &#x2014; Integrated Framework</i><i> (</i><i>2013</i><i>)</i><i>. </i>Based on the assessment using those criteria,<i> </i>our management concluded that as of December 31, 2019, our internal control over financial reporting was effective. The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019 has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which is included in Part II &#x201c;Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.&#x201d;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&#xa0;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">(c) <i>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</i>. There has been no change in our &#x201c;internal control over financial reporting&#x201d; as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act, during our most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
